text: In the retroactivity framework (Del Vecchio et al.), which strategy inserts a buffering stage, such as a phosphorylation-dephosphorylation cycle, between an upstream circuit and its downstream load?
choices: Truncating the guide RNA spacer to 17-18 nt
Adding degradation tags only to the downstream target protein
Switching to a two-input operator promoter
explanation: An insulation device, such as a phosphorylation-dephosphorylation amplifier stage, sits between circuit stages and buffers the upstream part from the loading effect of the downstream target, directly counteracting retroactivity. Truncated guide RNAs are a strategy for reducing CRISPR off-target effects, not retroactivity; degradation tags reduce steady-state titration but are a separate mitigation from insulation; and two-input operator promoters are an AND-gate implementation, unrelated to retroactivity mitigation.
